en: In 1937 Picasso was the most famous artist in the world.
zh: 1937年，畢卡索是世界上最著名的藝術家。
ja: 1937年、ピカソは世界で最も有名な芸術家でした。
local: In 1937 Picasso was the most famous artist in the world.
native: In 1937 Picasso was the most famous artist in the world.

en: A prolific innovator of art forms, he had already pioneered cubism, invented collage,
zh: 他是多產的藝術形式創新者，已經開創了立體主義，發明了拼貼藝術，
ja: 彼は多作な芸術形式の革新者であり、すでにキュビスムを開拓し、コラージュを発明していました。
local: A prolific innovator of art forms, he had already pioneered cubism, invented collage,
native: A prolific innovator of art forms, he had already pioneered cubism, invented collage,

en: and made major contributions to symbolism and surrealism.
zh: 並對象徵主義和超現實主義做出了重大貢獻。
ja: そして象徴主義やシュルレアリスムにも大きな貢献をしました。
local: and made major contributions to symbolism and surrealism.
native: and made major contributions to symbolism and surrealism.

en: And he was just about to create the most powerful anti-war painting in history.
zh: 他正準備創作歷史上最強烈的反戰畫作。
ja: そして彼は歴史上最も強力な反戦画をまさに創ろうとしていました。
local: And he was just about to create the most powerful anti-war painting in history.
native: And he was just about to create the most powerful anti-war painting in history.

en: Monday, April the 26th, 1937.
zh: 1937年4月26日，星期一。
ja: 1937年4月26日、月曜日。
local: Monday, April the 26th, 1937.
native: Monday, April the 26th, 1937.

en: German warplanes began appearing in the sky above the small busk village of Guernica.
zh: 德國戰機開始出現在小巴斯克村莊格爾尼卡的天空中。
ja: ドイツの戦闘機が小さなバスクの村ゲルニカの上空に現れ始めました。
local: German warplanes began appearing in the sky above the small busk village of Guernica.
native: German warplanes began appearing in the sky above the small busk village of Guernica.

en: It was 4.30pm, and the planes were here on behalf of General Franco's fascist regime,
zh: 當時是下午4點半，這些飛機代表佛朗哥將軍的法西斯政權來到這裡，
ja: 午後4時30分で、飛行機はフランコ将軍のファシスト政権を代表していました。
local: It was 4.30pm, and the planes were here on behalf of General Franco's fascist regime,
native: It was 4.30pm, and the planes were here on behalf of General Franco's fascist regime,

en: and as a macabre rehearsal for the Blitzkrieg tactics of World War II.
zh: 並作為第二次世界大戰閃電戰戰術的陰森彩排。
ja: そして第二次世界大戦の電撃戦戦術の不気味なリハーサルとしてでした。
local: and as a macabre rehearsal for the Blitzkrieg tactics of World War II.
native: and as a macabre rehearsal for the Blitzkrieg tactics of World War II.

en: The attack was timed to maximize civilian casualties.
zh: 這次攻擊的時間安排是為了最大化平民傷亡。
ja: 攻撃は民間人の犠牲者を最大化するために計画されました。
local: The attack was timed to maximize civilian casualties.
native: The attack was timed to maximize civilian casualties.

en: For over three hours, 25 bombers dropped 100,000 pounds of explosive and incendiary bombs on the village,
zh: 超過三個小時內，25架轟炸機向村莊投下了10萬磅的爆炸物和燃燒彈，
ja: 3時間以上にわたり、25機の爆撃機が村に10万ポンドの爆発物と焼夷弾を投下しました。
local: For over three hours, 25 bombers dropped 100,000 pounds of explosive and incendiary bombs on the village,
native: For over three hours, 25 bombers dropped 100,000 pounds of explosive and incendiary bombs on the village,

en: reducing it to rubble and killing a third of the population.
zh: 將村莊夷為廢墟，並殺死了三分之一的人口。
ja: 村は瓦礫の山となり、住民の3分の1が死亡しました。
local: reducing it to rubble and killing a third of the population.
native: reducing it to rubble and killing a third of the population.

en: This brutal and unprovoked attack shot the world.
zh: 這次殘酷且無端的攻擊震驚了世界。
ja: この残酷で不当な攻撃は世界を震撼させました。
local: This brutal and unprovoked attack shot the world.
native: This brutal and unprovoked attack shot the world.

en: He also inspired Picasso to produce a political painting that is as relevant today as it was when he produced it over 80 years ago.
zh: 這也激發了畢卡索創作一幅政治畫，至今仍具現實意義，正如80多年前他創作時一樣。
ja: これがピカソに政治的な絵画を制作させ、80年以上前に制作された時と同じくらい今日でも重要な作品となっています。
local: He also inspired Picasso to produce a political painting that is as relevant today as it was when he produced it over 80 years ago.
native: He also inspired Picasso to produce a political painting that is as relevant today as it was when he produced it over 80 years ago.

en: In 1936, a group of right-wing generals launched a military coup on the legally elected Spanish Republic
zh: 1936年，一群右翼將軍對合法選出的西班牙共和國發動了軍事政變，
ja: 1936年、右翼の将軍たちが合法的に選ばれたスペイン共和国に対して軍事クーデターを起こしました。
local: In 1936, a group of right-wing generals launched a military coup on the legally elected Spanish Republic
native: In 1936, a group of right-wing generals launched a military coup on the legally elected Spanish Republic

en: and started the Spanish Civil War.
zh: 並引發了西班牙內戰。
ja: そしてスペイン内戦が始まりました。
local: and started the Spanish Civil War.
native: and started the Spanish Civil War.

en: War had been going on for six months when Picasso was given a commission to produce a large-scale mural for the Spanish Republic's pavilion at the 1937 World's Fair in Paris,
zh: 當戰爭已持續六個月時，畢卡索接到委託，為1937年巴黎世界博覽會西班牙共和國館創作大型壁畫，
ja: 戦争が6か月続いていた時、ピカソは1937年のパリ万国博覧会のスペイン共和国館のために大規模な壁画を制作する依頼を受けました。
local: War had been going on for six months when Picasso was given a commission to produce a large-scale mural for the Spanish Republic's pavilion at the 1937 World's Fair in Paris,
native: War had been going on for six months when Picasso was given a commission to produce a large-scale mural for the Spanish Republic's pavilion at the 1937 World's Fair in Paris,

en: where Picasso was living.
zh: 當時畢卡索正居住於巴黎。
ja: ピカソはパリに住んでいました。
local: where Picasso was living.
native: where Picasso was living.

en: Picasso was famously apolitical and told the republicans, I don't do politics.
zh: 畢卡索以不涉政治聞名，他告訴共和派：「我不做政治。」
ja: ピカソは政治に関心がないことで有名で、共和派に「私は政治をしない」と言いました。
local: Picasso was famously apolitical and told the republicans, I don't do politics.
native: Picasso was famously apolitical and told the republicans, I don't do politics.

en: But after months of staring at a blank canvas, he was still struggling to come up with ideas.
zh: 但經過數月凝視空白畫布，他仍在努力構思。
ja: しかし、数か月間白紙のキャンバスを見つめた後も、彼はまだアイデアを思いつけずにいました。
local: But after months of staring at a blank canvas, he was still struggling to come up with ideas.
native: But after months of staring at a blank canvas, he was still struggling to come up with ideas.

en: History intervened, and Picasso found his subject.
zh: 歷史介入，畢卡索找到了他的主題。
ja: 歴史が介入し、ピカソは題材を見つけました。
local: History intervened, and Picasso found his subject.
native: History intervened, and Picasso found his subject.

en: Like the rest of the world, he opened his newspaper on April the 27th to find devastating images of the bombing of Gernica.
zh: 和世界其他人一樣，他在4月27日打開報紙，看到格爾尼卡轟炸的毀滅性畫面。
ja: 世界中の人々と同様に、彼は4月27日に新聞を開き、ゲルニカ爆撃の壊滅的な映像を目にしました。
local: Like the rest of the world, he opened his newspaper on April the 27th to find devastating images of the bombing of Gernica.
native: Like the rest of the world, he opened his newspaper on April the 27th to find devastating images of the bombing of Gernica.

en: Picasso was horrified and frantically started work on new sketches for the commission.
zh: 畢卡索感到震驚，瘋狂地開始為委託創作新素描。
ja: ピカソは恐怖に駆られ、委託作品のための新しいスケッチを必死に描き始めました。
local: Picasso was horrified and frantically started work on new sketches for the commission.
native: Picasso was horrified and frantically started work on new sketches for the commission.

en: He would complete the enormous painting in only three weeks.
zh: 他僅用三週就完成了這幅巨作。
ja: 彼はわずか3週間で巨大な絵画を完成させました。
local: He would complete the enormous painting in only three weeks.
native: He would complete the enormous painting in only three weeks.

en: Perhaps Picasso's greatest skill was reinvention.
zh: 或許畢卡索最大的才能是自我革新。
ja: おそらくピカソの最大の才能は再発明でした。
local: Perhaps Picasso's greatest skill was reinvention.
native: Perhaps Picasso's greatest skill was reinvention.

en: In Le Demois L. Davignon, he played with idealised female beauty,
zh: 在《Le Demois L. Davignon》中，他玩味理想化的女性美，
ja: 『ル・デモワゼル・L・ダヴィニョン』では、彼は理想化された女性の美しさを表現しました。
local: In Le Demois L. Davignon, he played with idealised female beauty,
native: In Le Demois L. Davignon, he played with idealised female beauty,

en: and in Gernica, he would reinvigorate the genre of historical painting.
zh: 而在《格爾尼卡》中，他重新賦予歷史畫類型新的生命。
ja: そして『ゲルニカ』では、彼は歴史画のジャンルに新たな活力を与えました。
local: and in Gernica, he would reinvigorate the genre of historical painting.
native: and in Gernica, he would reinvigorate the genre of historical painting.

en: The first thing you notice is the gigantic size.
zh: 你首先注意到的是它巨大的尺寸。
ja: 最初に目に入るのはその巨大なサイズです。
local: The first thing you notice is the gigantic size.
native: The first thing you notice is the gigantic size.

en: It is 4 metres by 8 metres, or 11 feet by 26 feet, and is one piece of material rather than several canvases sewn together.
zh: 它長4米寬8米，或11英尺乘26英尺，是一整塊材料，而非多塊畫布縫合而成。
ja: 4メートル×8メートル、または11フィート×26フィートの大きさで、複数のキャンバスを縫い合わせたものではなく、一枚の素材でできています。
local: It is 4 metres by 8 metres, or 11 feet by 26 feet, and is one piece of material rather than several canvases sewn together.
native: It is 4 metres by 8 metres, or 11 feet by 26 feet, and is one piece of material rather than several canvases sewn together.

en: After Paris, it was to be sent around the world to raise money for Spain.
zh: 巴黎展出後，它將被送往世界各地為西班牙募款。
ja: パリの後、スペインのための資金調達のために世界中を巡回しました。
local: After Paris, it was to be sent around the world to raise money for Spain.
native: After Paris, it was to be sent around the world to raise money for Spain.

en: Because of the size, each time it travelled, the canvas had to be removed from the stretcher, rolled up, packed and shipped.
zh: 由於尺寸，每次運輸時，畫布必須從畫架上取下，捲起，打包並運送。
ja: サイズのため、移動のたびにキャンバスを張る枠から外し、巻いて梱包し発送しなければなりませんでした。
local: Because of the size, each time it travelled, the canvas had to be removed from the stretcher, rolled up, packed and shipped.
native: Because of the size, each time it travelled, the canvas had to be removed from the stretcher, rolled up, packed and shipped.

en: Again and again.
zh: 一次又一次。
ja: 何度も何度も繰り返されました。
local: Again and again.
native: Again and again.

en: In that sense, we can compare Gernica to portable tapestries known in Spain as Sardgas.
zh: 從這個角度來看，我們可以將《格爾尼卡》比作西班牙稱為Sardgas的便攜式掛毯。
ja: その意味で、『ゲルニカ』はスペインでサルダガスと呼ばれる携帯用のタペストリーに例えられます。
local: In that sense, we can compare Gernica to portable tapestries known in Spain as Sardgas.
native: In that sense, we can compare Gernica to portable tapestries known in Spain as Sardgas.

en: They were used in Spain and other countries from the 15th century as temporary curtains, banners and wall hangings during Lent.
zh: 它們從15世紀起在西班牙及其他國家用作臨時窗簾、橫幅和四旬期的壁掛。
ja: 15世紀からスペインや他の国々で、四旬節の間の仮設カーテンやバナー、壁掛けとして使われていました。
local: They were used in Spain and other countries from the 15th century as temporary curtains, banners and wall hangings during Lent.
native: They were used in Spain and other countries from the 15th century as temporary curtains, banners and wall hangings during Lent.

en: Like Gernica, it was propaganda, but of a religious kind.
zh: 像《格爾尼卡》一樣，它是宣傳，但屬於宗教性質的。
ja: 『ゲルニカ』のように、それはプロパガンダでしたが、宗教的なものでした。
local: Like Gernica, it was propaganda, but of a religious kind.
native: Like Gernica, it was propaganda, but of a religious kind.

en: He primed the canvas with several layers of reflective lead white, an antiquated paint base used by Leonardo da Vinci.
zh: 他用多層反光的鉛白底漆處理畫布，這是達文西使用的古老底漆。
ja: 彼はキャンバスにレオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチが使った古風な塗料である反射性の鉛白を何層も塗りました。
local: He primed the canvas with several layers of reflective lead white, an antiquated paint base used by Leonardo da Vinci.
native: He primed the canvas with several layers of reflective lead white, an antiquated paint base used by Leonardo da Vinci.

en: Picasso wanted a reflective surface to paint on.
zh: 畢卡索想要一個反光的繪畫表面。
ja: ピカソは反射する表面に絵を描きたかったのです。
local: Picasso wanted a reflective surface to paint on.
native: Picasso wanted a reflective surface to paint on.

en: The ground layer was important as it was to form part of the composition.
zh: 底層很重要，因為它將成為構圖的一部分。
ja: 下地の層は構図の一部を形成するため重要でした。
local: The ground layer was important as it was to form part of the composition.
native: The ground layer was important as it was to form part of the composition.

en: He used normal household paint with a minimum amount of gloss, so the white parts of the painting are luminous, whereas the blacks are matte black.
zh: 他使用普通家用漆，光澤度最低，因此畫中的白色部分是發光的，而黑色部分是啞光黑。
ja: 彼は通常の家庭用塗料を使い、光沢を最小限に抑えたため、絵の白い部分は輝き、黒い部分はマットな黒になっています。
local: He used normal household paint with a minimum amount of gloss, so the white parts of the painting are luminous, whereas the blacks are matte black.
native: He used normal household paint with a minimum amount of gloss, so the white parts of the painting are luminous, whereas the blacks are matte black.

en: The speed at which he paints leaves splashes, such as here, and mistakes, adding to the urgency of the painting.
zh: 他繪畫的速度留下了飛濺和錯誤，如此增添了畫作的緊迫感。
ja: 彼の描く速さは、ここにあるような飛び散りやミスを残し、絵の緊迫感を増しています。
local: The speed at which he paints leaves splashes, such as here, and mistakes, adding to the urgency of the painting.
native: The speed at which he paints leaves splashes, such as here, and mistakes, adding to the urgency of the painting.

en: The other thing you notice straight away is the absence of colour.
zh: 你立刻注意到的另一件事是缺乏色彩。
ja: もう一つすぐに気づくのは色彩の欠如です。
local: The other thing you notice straight away is the absence of colour.
native: The other thing you notice straight away is the absence of colour.

en: But in 1937, people only experienced current events in black and white.
zh: 但在1937年，人們只能以黑白方式接收當時的新聞。
ja: しかし1937年、人々はニュースを白黒でしか体験できませんでした。
local: But in 1937, people only experienced current events in black and white.
native: But in 1937, people only experienced current events in black and white.

en: And Gernica was as current as you could get.
zh: 而《格爾尼卡》是當時最即時的表現。
ja: そして『ゲルニカ』は当時の最も最新の出来事を表していました。
local: And Gernica was as current as you could get.
native: And Gernica was as current as you could get.

en: Picasso himself saw the Spanish Civil War play out in black and white in newspapers, and he even gives us a suggestion of torn newsprint in the white
zh: 畢卡索本人在報紙上以黑白方式看到西班牙內戰的發展，他甚至在白色部分暗示了撕裂的報紙。
ja: ピカソ自身もスペイン内戦を新聞の白黒写真で見ており、白い部分には破れた新聞紙のような表現もあります。
local: Picasso himself saw the Spanish Civil War play out in black and white in newspapers, and he even gives us a suggestion of torn newsprint in the white
native: Picasso himself saw the Spanish Civil War play out in black and white in newspapers, and he even gives us a suggestion of torn newsprint in the white

en: and newsprint in the horses chainmail.
zh: 以及馬匹鎖甲上的報紙印刷字樣。
ja: そして馬の鎖かたびらには新聞の印刷が表現されています。
local: and newsprint in the horses chainmail.
native: and newsprint in the horses chainmail.

en: Picasso was the magpie of the art world with an encyclopedic knowledge of art history.
zh: 畢卡索是藝術界的喜鵲，擁有博學的藝術史知識。
ja: ピカソは芸術界のカササギであり、博識な美術史の知識を持っていました。
local: Picasso was the magpie of the art world with an encyclopedic knowledge of art history.
native: Picasso was the magpie of the art world with an encyclopedic knowledge of art history.

en: With Gernica, it is these visual references that anchor the work.
zh: 在《格爾尼卡》中，正是這些視覺參考穩固了作品。
ja: 『ゲルニカ』では、これらの視覚的な参照が作品の基盤となっています。
local: With Gernica, it is these visual references that anchor the work.
native: With Gernica, it is these visual references that anchor the work.

en: Peter Paul Rubens was an artist Picasso loved, and Rubens painting an allegory showing the effects of war from 1638 is the work that most inspired Picasso's Gernica.
zh: 彼得·保羅·魯本斯是畢卡索喜愛的藝術家，魯本斯1638年描繪戰爭影響的寓言畫作最啟發了畢卡索的《格爾尼卡》。
ja: ピーター・ポール・ルーベンスはピカソが愛した画家で、1638年の戦争の影響を描いた寓意画が『ゲルニカ』に最も影響を与えました。
local: Peter Paul Rubens was an artist Picasso loved, and Rubens painting an allegory showing the effects of war from 1638 is the work that most inspired Picasso's Gernica.
native: Peter Paul Rubens was an artist Picasso loved, and Rubens painting an allegory showing the effects of war from 1638 is the work that most inspired Picasso's Gernica.

en: If we flip Rubens painting, we can see the similarities in composition.
zh: 如果我們將魯本斯的畫作翻轉，可以看到構圖上的相似之處。
ja: ルーベンスの絵を反転させると、構図の類似点が見られます。
local: If we flip Rubens painting, we can see the similarities in composition.
native: If we flip Rubens painting, we can see the similarities in composition.

en: From left to right, we get a weeping woman with a child in her arms.
zh: 從左到右，我們看到一位懷抱孩子的哭泣婦女。
ja: 左から右へ、子供を抱く泣いている女性がいます。
local: From left to right, we get a weeping woman with a child in her arms.
native: From left to right, we get a weeping woman with a child in her arms.

en: A flying fury of war holding out a torch, and a woman facing the heavens without stretched arms.
zh: 一位揮舞火炬的戰爭狂怒者，以及一位面向天空但未伸展雙臂的婦女。
ja: 戦争の怒りが松明を掲げ、腕を伸ばさず天を仰ぐ女性がいます。
local: A flying fury of war holding out a torch, and a woman facing the heavens without stretched arms.
native: A flying fury of war holding out a torch, and a woman facing the heavens without stretched arms.

en: We can also compare the weeping woman to Michelangelo's lapierter, and the flying fury to Prudon's allegory of justice.
zh: 我們還可以將哭泣的婦女與米開朗基羅的《拉皮埃特》相比較，將飛翔的狂怒者與普魯東的正義寓言相比較。
ja: 泣く女性はミケランジェロの『ラピエール』に、飛ぶ怒りはプリュドンの正義の寓意に例えられます。
local: We can also compare the weeping woman to Michelangelo's lapierter, and the flying fury to Prudon's allegory of justice.
native: We can also compare the weeping woman to Michelangelo's lapierter, and the flying fury to Prudon's allegory of justice.

en: Goya, an artist Picasso admired, is another inspiration.
zh: 戈雅是畢卡索敬佩的藝術家，也是另一個靈感來源。
ja: ゴヤはピカソが敬愛した画家で、別のインスピレーションの源です。
local: Goya, an artist Picasso admired, is another inspiration.
native: Goya, an artist Picasso admired, is another inspiration.

en: Third of May 1808 also depicts a nighttime massacre.
zh: 《1808年5月3日》也描繪了一場夜間大屠殺。
ja: 『1808年5月3日』も夜の虐殺を描いています。
local: Third of May 1808 also depicts a nighttime massacre.
native: Third of May 1808 also depicts a nighttime massacre.

en: The central figure's pose is reminiscent of the screaming woman, and inevitably, both figures can be compared to a crucifixion.
zh: 中央人物的姿勢讓人想起尖叫的婦女，兩者都不可避免地被比作受難。
ja: 中央の人物のポーズは叫ぶ女性を思わせ、どちらも十字架の磔刑に例えられます。
local: The central figure's pose is reminiscent of the screaming woman, and inevitably, both figures can be compared to a crucifixion.
native: The central figure's pose is reminiscent of the screaming woman, and inevitably, both figures can be compared to a crucifixion.

en: And in both paintings, we find the sign of the stick martyr.
zh: 在兩幅畫中，我們都能看到棍子殉道者的象徵。
ja: 両方の絵に、棒の殉教者のサインが見られます。
local: And in both paintings, we find the sign of the stick martyr.
native: And in both paintings, we find the sign of the stick martyr.

en: There are also comparisons to be made with his own earlier work.
zh: 也可以將其與他早期的作品做比較。
ja: 彼自身の初期作品とも比較できます。
local: There are also comparisons to be made with his own earlier work.
native: There are also comparisons to be made with his own earlier work.

en: But there is more than just iconographic inspiration here.
zh: 但這裡不僅僅是圖像符號的靈感。
ja: しかし、ここには単なる図像的なインスピレーション以上のものがあります。
local: But there is more than just iconographic inspiration here.
native: But there is more than just iconographic inspiration here.

en: Surprisingly, Picasso's Gernica has no specific references to the actual bombing of the Basque village.
zh: 令人驚訝的是，畢卡索的《格爾尼卡》沒有具體提及巴斯克村莊的實際轟炸。
ja: 驚くべきことに、ピカソの『ゲルニカ』にはバスクの村の実際の爆撃への具体的な言及はありません。
local: Surprisingly, Picasso's Gernica has no specific references to the actual bombing of the Basque village.
native: Surprisingly, Picasso's Gernica has no specific references to the actual bombing of the Basque village.

en: He has created a fictitious scene whose intensity evokes the suffering of all wars.
zh: 他創造了一個虛構場景，其強烈程度喚起了所有戰爭的苦難。
ja: 彼は架空の場面を作り出し、その激しさがすべての戦争の苦しみを呼び起こします。
local: He has created a fictitious scene whose intensity evokes the suffering of all wars.
native: He has created a fictitious scene whose intensity evokes the suffering of all wars.

en: Gernica is an allegorical painting.
zh: 《格爾尼卡》是一幅寓言畫。
ja: 『ゲルニカ』は寓意画です。
local: Gernica is an allegorical painting.
native: Gernica is an allegorical painting.

en: In the same way Rubens work is an allegorical response to the Thirty Years' War.
zh: 就像魯本斯的作品是對三十年戰爭的寓言回應一樣。
ja: ルーベンスの作品が三十年戦争への寓意的な応答であるのと同様です。
local: In the same way Rubens work is an allegorical response to the Thirty Years' War.
native: In the same way Rubens work is an allegorical response to the Thirty Years' War.

en: The scene is intentionally chaotic to evoke the horror and confusion of war.
zh: 場景故意混亂，以喚起戰爭的恐怖與混亂。
ja: この場面は戦争の恐怖と混乱を呼び起こすために意図的に混沌としています。
local: The scene is intentionally chaotic to evoke the horror and confusion of war.
native: The scene is intentionally chaotic to evoke the horror and confusion of war.

en: We are thrown into apocalyptic action by characters overlap and intersect.
zh: 人物重疊交錯，將我們投入末日般的行動中。
ja: 登場人物が重なり合い交差することで、私たちは黙示録的な行動に投げ込まれます。
local: We are thrown into apocalyptic action by characters overlap and intersect.
native: We are thrown into apocalyptic action by characters overlap and intersect.

en: Destruction, violent death, and mutilation are everywhere.
zh: 破壞、暴力死亡和肢解無處不在。
ja: 破壊、激しい死、そして切断が至る所にあります。
local: Destruction, violent death, and mutilation are everywhere.
native: Destruction, violent death, and mutilation are everywhere.

en: Despite Picasso's avant-garde qualities, he trained as a classical artist.
zh: 儘管畢卡索具有前衛特質，他仍接受過古典藝術訓練。
ja: ピカソは前衛的な特徴を持ちながらも、古典的な芸術家として訓練を受けました。
local: Despite Picasso's avant-garde qualities, he trained as a classical artist.
native: Despite Picasso's avant-garde qualities, he trained as a classical artist.

en: And Gernica uses classical language.
zh: 《格爾尼卡》使用了古典語言。
ja: そして『ゲルニカ』は古典的な表現を用いています。
local: And Gernica uses classical language.
native: And Gernica uses classical language.

en: Despite the chaos, there is in fact a clear visual order.
zh: 儘管混亂，實際上有明確的視覺秩序。
ja: 混沌の中にも明確な視覚的秩序があります。
local: Despite the chaos, there is in fact a clear visual order.
native: Despite the chaos, there is in fact a clear visual order.

en: Picasso balances the composition by organizing the figures into three vertical groupings, moving left to right.
zh: 畢卡索將人物分成三個垂直群組，從左到右排列，平衡了構圖。
ja: ピカソは人物を左から右へ三つの縦のグループに分けて構図のバランスをとっています。
local: Picasso balances the composition by organizing the figures into three vertical groupings, moving left to right.
native: Picasso balances the composition by organizing the figures into three vertical groupings, moving left to right.

en: While the central figures are stabilized within a large triangle of light.
zh: 中央人物穩定地置於一個大光三角形中。
ja: 中央の人物は大きな光の三角形の中で安定しています。
local: While the central figures are stabilized within a large triangle of light.
native: While the central figures are stabilized within a large triangle of light.

en: To the far left we see a wide-eyed bull with a dark body and white head.
zh: 最左邊是一頭睜大眼睛、身體黑暗、頭部白色的公牛。
ja: 一番左には、目を見開いた黒い体と白い頭の雄牛がいます。
local: To the far left we see a wide-eyed bull with a dark body and white head.
native: To the far left we see a wide-eyed bull with a dark body and white head.

en: The horse and bull are images Picasso used his entire career, part of the life and death ritual of Spanish bullfights.
zh: 馬和牛是畢卡索整個職業生涯中使用的形象，是西班牙鬥牛生死儀式的一部分。
ja: 馬と雄牛はピカソが生涯にわたり使ったイメージで、スペインの闘牛の生と死の儀式の一部です。
local: The horse and bull are images Picasso used his entire career, part of the life and death ritual of Spanish bullfights.
native: The horse and bull are images Picasso used his entire career, part of the life and death ritual of Spanish bullfights.

en: The bull is the only figure that is looking at us, the viewer.
zh: 公牛是唯一直視我們觀眾的形象。
ja: 雄牛は私たち観客を見つめる唯一の人物です。
local: The bull is the only figure that is looking at us, the viewer.
native: The bull is the only figure that is looking at us, the viewer.

en: Picasso himself thought of the bull as representing brutality and darkness.
zh: 畢卡索本人認為公牛代表野蠻和黑暗。
ja: ピカソ自身は雄牛を残虐さと闇の象徴と考えていました。
local: Picasso himself thought of the bull as representing brutality and darkness.
native: Picasso himself thought of the bull as representing brutality and darkness.

en: Days is cold and detached.
zh: 它冷漠且疏離。
ja: それは冷たく、距離を置いています。
local: Days is cold and detached.
native: Days is cold and detached.

en: It has come to be seen as representing fascism or Franco himself.
zh: 它被視為代表法西斯主義或佛朗哥本人。
ja: それはファシズムやフランコ自身を象徴すると見なされています。
local: It has come to be seen as representing fascism or Franco himself.
native: It has come to be seen as representing fascism or Franco himself.

en: It's tale smolders like the smoking remains of Gernica.
zh: 它的尾巴像格爾尼卡冒煙的殘骸一樣冒煙。
ja: その尾はゲルニカの煙る残骸のように燻っています。
local: It's tale smolders like the smoking remains of Gernica.
native: It's tale smolders like the smoking remains of Gernica.

en: Underneath the bull, a woman is holding a dead child, screaming towards the heavens.
zh: 在公牛下方，一名婦女抱著一個死去的孩子，向天空尖叫。
ja: 雄牛の下には、死んだ子供を抱き、天に向かって叫ぶ女性がいます。
local: Underneath the bull, a woman is holding a dead child, screaming towards the heavens.
native: Underneath the bull, a woman is holding a dead child, screaming towards the heavens.

en: Her bare breasts that once fed her child are exposed, and her eyes are in the shape of tears.
zh: 她曾哺育孩子的裸露乳房暴露出來，眼睛呈淚珠形狀。
ja: かつて子供に授乳していた裸の胸が露出し、目は涙の形をしています。
local: Her bare breasts that once fed her child are exposed, and her eyes are in the shape of tears.
native: Her bare breasts that once fed her child are exposed, and her eyes are in the shape of tears.

en: She is a secular virgin and child tainted by war.
zh: 她是一位被戰爭玷污的世俗聖母與孩子。
ja: 彼女は戦争に汚された世俗の聖母と子供です。
local: She is a secular virgin and child tainted by war.
native: She is a secular virgin and child tainted by war.

en: Further down lies a dead soldier, representing both futility and hope.
zh: 更下方躺著一名死去的士兵，象徵著徒勞與希望。
ja: さらに下には死んだ兵士が横たわり、無意味さと希望の両方を表しています。
local: Further down lies a dead soldier, representing both futility and hope.
native: Further down lies a dead soldier, representing both futility and hope.

en: His disjointed parts are strewn about the floor.
zh: 他支離破碎的身體部位散落在地板上。
ja: 彼のバラバラになった体の部分が床に散らばっています。
local: His disjointed parts are strewn about the floor.
ja_pron: Kare no barabara ni natta karada no bubun ga yuka ni chirabatte imasu.
native: His disjointed parts are strewn about the floor.

en: One severed arm carries a broken sword of failure, from which grows a white poppy.
zh: 一隻斷臂握著失敗的斷劍，劍上長出一朵白色罌粟花。
ja: 一本切断された腕が失敗の折れた剣を持っており、その剣から白いケシの花が咲いています。
local: One severed arm carries a broken sword of failure, from which grows a white poppy.
ja_pron: Ippon setsudan sareta ude ga shippai no oreta ken o motte ori, sono ken kara shiroi keshi no hana ga saite imasu.
native: One severed arm carries a broken sword of failure, from which grows a white poppy.

en: The symbol of remembrance and hope.
zh: 這是紀念與希望的象徵。
ja: それは記憶と希望の象徴です。
local: The symbol of remembrance and hope.
ja_pron: Sore wa kioku to kibō no shōchō desu.
native: The symbol of remembrance and hope.

en: In his other hand, the signs of the stigmata represent the ultimate sacrifice.
zh: 在他的另一隻手上，聖痕的標誌象徵著最終的犧牲。
ja: もう一方の手には、聖痕の印が究極の犠牲を表しています。
local: In his other hand, the signs of the stigmata represent the ultimate sacrifice.
ja_pron: Mō ippō no te ni wa, seikon no shirushi ga kyūkyoku no gisei o arawashite imasu.
native: In his other hand, the signs of the stigmata represent the ultimate sacrifice.

en: Between the bull and the horse, we can just about see a dove.
zh: 在公牛和馬之間，我們幾乎可以看到一隻鴿子。
ja: 雄牛と馬の間に、かろうじて鳩が見えます。
local: Between the bull and the horse, we can just about see a dove.
ja_pron: Oushi to uma no aida ni, karōjite hato ga miemasu.
native: Between the bull and the horse, we can just about see a dove.

en: Normally a representation of peace, Picasso's version with its pained expression and broken body suggests that pieces all but destroyed.
zh: 鴿子通常象徵和平，但畢卡索的版本帶著痛苦的表情和破碎的身體，暗示著幾乎被摧毀的碎片。
ja: 通常は平和の象徴である鳩ですが、ピカソの作品では痛ましい表情と壊れた体で、ほとんど破壊された断片を示しています。
local: Normally a representation of peace, Picasso's version with its pained expression and broken body suggests that pieces all but destroyed.
ja_pron: Tsūjō wa heiwa no shōchō de aru hato desu ga, Pikaso no sakuhin de wa itamashii hyōjō to kowareta karada de, hotondo hakai sareta danpen o shimeshite imasu.
native: Normally a representation of peace, Picasso's version with its pained expression and broken body suggests that pieces all but destroyed.

en: The light bulb is the single image of 20th century technology and has multiple meanings.
zh: 電燈泡是20世紀科技的唯一象徵，且具有多重意義。
ja: 電球は20世紀の技術の象徴であり、複数の意味を持っています。
local: The light bulb is the single image of 20th century technology and has multiple meanings.
ja_pron: Denkyū wa nijusseiki no gijutsu no shōchō de ari, fukusū no imi o motte imasu.
native: The light bulb is the single image of 20th century technology and has multiple meanings.

en: Perhaps it is the eye of God overlooking the madness of war.
zh: 也許它是上帝之眼，俯瞰戰爭的瘋狂。
ja: おそらくそれは戦争の狂気を見下ろす神の目でしょう。
local: Perhaps it is the eye of God overlooking the madness of war.
ja_pron: Osoraku sore wa sensō no kyōki o miorosu kami no me deshō.
native: Perhaps it is the eye of God overlooking the madness of war.

en: The more accepted interpretation is that it represents the technology that destroyed Gernica.
zh: 較被接受的解釋是它代表摧毀格爾尼卡的科技。
ja: より一般的な解釈は、それがゲルニカを破壊した技術を表しているということです。
local: The more accepted interpretation is that it represents the technology that destroyed Gernica.
ja_pron: Yori ippanteki na kaishaku wa, sore ga Gerunika o hakai shita gijutsu o arawashite iru to iu koto desu.
native: The more accepted interpretation is that it represents the technology that destroyed Gernica.

en: In Spanish, the word for light bulb is bombia, which brings to mind the word bomb.
zh: 在西班牙語中，電燈泡的詞是 bombia，讓人聯想到炸彈這個詞。
ja: スペイン語で電球は「bombia」と言い、爆弾を連想させます。
local: In Spanish, the word for light bulb is bombia, which brings to mind the word bomb.
ja_pron: Supeingo de denkyū wa 'bombia' to ii, bakudan o rensō sasemasu.
native: In Spanish, the word for light bulb is bombia, which brings to mind the word bomb.

en: The screaming horse at the center is collapsing from its gaping wound, but its head remains upward as it struggles to live.
zh: 中央尖叫的馬因巨大的傷口而倒下，但牠的頭仍然向上，努力求生。
ja: 中央の叫んでいる馬は大きな傷から倒れていますが、頭は上を向いたまま生きようとしています。
local: The screaming horse at the center is collapsing from its gaping wound, but its head remains upward as it struggles to live.
ja_pron: Chūō no sakende iru uma wa ōkina kizu kara taorete imasu ga, atama wa ue o muita mama ikiyō to shite imasu.
native: The screaming horse at the center is collapsing from its gaping wound, but its head remains upward as it struggles to live.

en: You can almost hear those ear piercing screams.
zh: 你幾乎能聽見那刺耳的尖叫聲。
ja: その耳をつんざくような叫び声がほとんど聞こえるようです。
local: You can almost hear those ear piercing screams.
ja_pron: Sono mimi o tsunzaku yō na sakebigoe ga hotondo kikoeru yō desu.
native: You can almost hear those ear piercing screams.

en: Picasso himself saw the terrorized horse as the people of Gernica.
zh: 畢卡索本人將那匹受驚的馬視為格爾尼卡的人民。
ja: ピカソ自身は恐怖におののく馬をゲルニカの人々と見なしました。
local: Picasso himself saw the terrorized horse as the people of Gernica.
ja_pron: Pikaso jishin wa kyōfu ni ononoku uma o Gerunika no hitobito to minamashita.
native: Picasso himself saw the terrorized horse as the people of Gernica.

en: The burning woman is perhaps the strongest representation of the painting's anti-war feeling.
zh: 燃燒的女人或許是這幅畫反戰情感最強烈的象徵。
ja: 燃えている女性は、この絵の反戦感情を最も強く表現しているかもしれません。
local: The burning woman is perhaps the strongest representation of the painting's anti-war feeling.
ja_pron: Moete iru josei wa, kono e no hansen kanjō o mottomo tsuyoku hyōgen shite iru kamoshiremasen.
native: The burning woman is perhaps the strongest representation of the painting's anti-war feeling.

en: A woman is trapped in a burning building, pleading at the sky, perhaps to God, perhaps to the German planes to stop the destruction.
zh: 一名女子被困在燃燒的建築物中，向天空哀求，或許是向上帝，或許是向德國飛機請求停止破壞。
ja: 女性が燃える建物に閉じ込められ、空に懇願しています。おそらく神に、あるいはドイツの飛行機に破壊をやめるように。
local: A woman is trapped in a burning building, pleading at the sky, perhaps to God, perhaps to the German planes to stop the destruction.
ja_pron: Josei ga moeru tatemono ni tojikomerare, sora ni kongan shite imasu. Osoraku kami ni, aruiwa Doitsu no hikōki ni hakai o yameru yō ni.
native: A woman is trapped in a burning building, pleading at the sky, perhaps to God, perhaps to the German planes to stop the destruction.

en: As she does so, the building continues to burn and crumble around her.
zh: 當她這樣做時，建築物繼續在她周圍燃燒並崩塌。
ja: 彼女がそうしている間も、建物は彼女の周りで燃え続け、崩れています。
local: As she does so, the building continues to burn and crumble around her.
ja_pron: Kanojo ga sō shite iru aida mo, tatemono wa kanojo no mawari de moe tsudzuke, kuzurete imasu.
native: As she does so, the building continues to burn and crumble around her.

en: Death is inevitable.
zh: 死亡是不可避免的。
ja: 死は避けられません。
local: Death is inevitable.
ja_pron: Shi wa sakeraremasen.
native: Death is inevitable.

en: Another terrified woman with an injured leg bleeding from the knee and trying to stop the blood with her hand.
zh: 另一名受驚的女子，腿部受傷，膝蓋流血，試圖用手止血。
ja: もう一人の恐怖におののく女性は、膝から出血している負傷した脚を手で止めようとしています。
local: Another terrified woman with an injured leg bleeding from the knee and trying to stop the blood with her hand.
ja_pron: Mō hitori no kyōfu ni ononoku josei wa, hiza kara shukketsu shite iru fushō shita ashi o te de tomeyō to shite imasu.
native: Another terrified woman with an injured leg bleeding from the knee and trying to stop the blood with her hand.

en: She is looking longingly towards the oil lamp.
zh: 她渴望地望向油燈。
ja: 彼女は切望するように油灯の方を見ています。
local: She is looking longingly towards the oil lamp.
ja_pron: Kanojo wa setsubō suru yō ni yutō no hō o mite imasu.
native: She is looking longingly towards the oil lamp.

en: It is actually the oil lamp that is the source of light in the scene, and not the electric light bulb.
zh: 實際上，場景中的光源是油燈，而非電燈泡。
ja: 実際には、この場面の光源は電球ではなく油灯です。
local: It is actually the oil lamp that is the source of light in the scene, and not the electric light bulb.
ja_pron: Jissai ni wa, kono bamen no kōgen wa denkyū de wa naku yutō desu.
native: It is actually the oil lamp that is the source of light in the scene, and not the electric light bulb.

en: The tiny flame is hope, and it is strong enough to shed light upon the entire scene.
zh: 微小的火焰是希望，足以照亮整個場景。
ja: 小さな炎は希望であり、場面全体を照らすのに十分な強さです。
local: The tiny flame is hope, and it is strong enough to shed light upon the entire scene.
ja_pron: Chīsana honō wa kibō de ari, bamen zentai o terasu no ni jūbun na tsuyosa desu.
native: The tiny flame is hope, and it is strong enough to shed light upon the entire scene.

en: It is the only sliver of hope in the painting, and is thought to represent the spirit of the Spanish Republic.
zh: 它是畫中唯一的一線希望，被認為代表西班牙共和國的精神。
ja: それは絵画の中で唯一の希望のかけらであり、スペイン共和国の精神を表していると考えられています。
local: It is the only sliver of hope in the painting, and is thought to represent the spirit of the Spanish Republic.
ja_pron: Sore wa kaiga no naka de yuiitsu no kibō no kakera de ari, Supein Kyōwakoku no seishin o arawashite iru to kangaerarete imasu.
native: It is the only sliver of hope in the painting, and is thought to represent the spirit of the Spanish Republic.

en: Gernica is not supposed to have a singular interpretation.
zh: 《格爾尼卡》不應該只有單一的詮釋。
ja: ゲルニカは一つの解釈だけを持つべきではありません。
local: Gernica is not supposed to have a singular interpretation.
ja_pron: Gerunika wa hitotsu no kaishaku dake o motsu beki de wa arimasen.
native: Gernica is not supposed to have a singular interpretation.

en: As Picasso said, we all know that art is not truth.
zh: 正如畢卡索所說，我們都知道藝術不是事實。
ja: ピカソが言ったように、私たちは皆、芸術が真実ではないことを知っています。
local: As Picasso said, we all know that art is not truth.
ja_pron: Pikaso ga itta yō ni, watashitachi wa mina, geijutsu ga shinjitsu de wa nai koto o shitte imasu.
native: As Picasso said, we all know that art is not truth.

en: Art is a lie that makes us realise truth.
zh: 藝術是一種讓我們認識真理的謊言。
ja: 芸術は私たちに真実を気づかせる嘘です。
local: Art is a lie that makes us realise truth.
ja_pron: Geijutsu wa watashitachi ni shinjitsu o kizukaseru uso desu.
native: Art is a lie that makes us realise truth.

en: Gernica's ambiguity and lack of specific historical detail make the painting timeless.
zh: 《格爾尼卡》的模糊性和缺乏具體歷史細節使這幅畫具有永恆的價值。
ja: ゲルニカの曖昧さと具体的な歴史的詳細の欠如が、この絵を時代を超えたものにしています。
local: Gernica's ambiguity and lack of specific historical detail make the painting timeless.
ja_pron: Gerunika no aimai-sa to gutaiteki na rekishiteki shōsai no ketsujo ga, kono e o jidai o koeta mono ni shite imasu.
native: Gernica's ambiguity and lack of specific historical detail make the painting timeless.

en: Picasso worked on the painting for 35 days, and finished it on the 4th June 1937.
zh: 畢卡索花了35天完成這幅畫，於1937年6月4日完成。
ja: ピカソはこの絵に35日間取り組み、1937年6月4日に完成させました。
local: Picasso worked on the painting for 35 days, and finished it on the 4th June 1937.
ja_pron: Pikaso wa kono e ni sanjūgo-nichikan torikumi, 1937-nen 6-gatsu 4-ka ni kansei saremashita.
native: Picasso worked on the painting for 35 days, and finished it on the 4th June 1937.

en: When it was unveiled at the Paris Expo, the public reaction was mixed.
zh: 當它在巴黎博覽會首次展出時，公眾反應不一。
ja: パリ万博で公開されたとき、一般の反応は賛否両論でした。
local: When it was unveiled at the Paris Expo, the public reaction was mixed.
ja_pron: Pari Banpaku de kōkai sareta toki, ippan no hannō wa sanpi ryōron deshita.
native: When it was unveiled at the Paris Expo, the public reaction was mixed.

en: It was two avant-garde for the Spanish officials who preferred another more traditional painting that they had also commissioned.
zh: 對於西班牙官員來說，它太過前衛，他們更喜歡另一幅他們也委託的更傳統的畫作。
ja: それはスペインの役人にはあまりにも前衛的すぎて、彼らは別のより伝統的な絵画を好み、それも委託していました。
local: It was two avant-garde for the Spanish officials who preferred another more traditional painting that they had also commissioned.
ja_pron: Sore wa Supein no yakunin ni wa amari ni mo zen'ei-teki sugite, karera wa betsu no yori dentō-teki na kaiga o konomi, sore mo itaku shite imashita.
native: It was two avant-garde for the Spanish officials who preferred another more traditional painting that they had also commissioned.

en: By Haudacio Ferre de Mogado.
zh: 由豪達西奧·費雷·德·莫加多創作。
ja: ハウダシオ・フェレ・デ・モガドによる作品です。
local: By Haudacio Ferre de Mogado.
ja_pron: Haudashio Fere de Mogado ni yoru sakuhin desu.
native: By Haudacio Ferre de Mogado.

en: However, after Paris, Gernica's reputation started to grow steadily as it travelled the world to raise money for the Republican cause.
zh: 然而，在巴黎之後，格爾尼卡的聲譽開始穩定增長，隨著它巡迴世界為共和黨事業籌款。
ja: しかし、パリの後、ゲルニカの評判は共和党のための資金を集めるために世界を巡るにつれて着実に高まり始めました。
local: However, after Paris, Gernica's reputation started to grow steadily as it travelled the world to raise money for the Republican cause.
ja_pron: Shikashi, Pari no ato, Gerunika no hyōban wa Kyōwatō no tame no shikin o atsumeru tame ni sekai o meguru ni tsurete chakujitsu ni takamari hajimemashita.
native: However, after Paris, Gernica's reputation started to grow steadily as it travelled the world to raise money for the Republican cause.

en: The start of the Second World War made its imagery more recognisable and painfully familiar.
zh: 第二次世界大戰的開始使其形象更加易於識別且令人痛苦地熟悉。
ja: 第二次世界大戦の始まりは、そのイメージをより認識しやすく、痛ましいほど馴染み深いものにしました。
local: The start of the Second World War made its imagery more recognisable and painfully familiar.
ja_pron: Dainiji Sekai Taisen no hajimari wa, sono imēji o yori ninshiki shi yasuku, itamashii hodo najimi bukai mono ni shimashita.
native: The start of the Second World War made its imagery more recognisable and painfully familiar.

en: Picasso refused to allow the painting to be seen in Spain while Franco ruled, and Gernica was sent on another tour.
zh: 在佛朗哥統治期間，畢卡索拒絕讓這幅畫在西班牙展出，格爾尼卡被送往另一個巡迴展。
ja: フランコが支配している間、ピカソはこの絵がスペインで見られることを拒否し、ゲルニカは別の巡回展に送られました。
local: Picasso refused to allow the painting to be seen in Spain while Franco ruled, and Gernica was sent on another tour.
ja_pron: Furanko ga shihaishite iru aida, Pikaso wa kono e ga Supein de mirareru koto o kyohi shi, Gerunika wa betsu no junkaiten ni okuraremashita.
native: Picasso refused to allow the painting to be seen in Spain while Franco ruled, and Gernica was sent on another tour.

en: This time to the United States to raise money for Spanish refugees fleeing fascism.
zh: 這次是前往美國為逃離法西斯主義的西班牙難民籌款。
ja: 今回はファシズムから逃れるスペイン難民のために資金を集めるためにアメリカ合衆国へ送り出されました。
local: This time to the United States to raise money for Spanish refugees fleeing fascism.
ja_pron: Konkai wa fashizumu kara nogareru Supein nanmin no tame ni shikin o atsumeru tame ni Amerika Gasshūkoku e okuridasa remashita.
native: This time to the United States to raise money for Spanish refugees fleeing fascism.

en: By 1940, it was at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, where it stayed on semi-permanent display.
zh: 到了1940年，它被安置在紐約現代藝術博物館，並在那裡半永久展出。
ja: 1940年までに、それはニューヨークの近代美術館にあり、そこで半永久的に展示されました。
local: By 1940, it was at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, where it stayed on semi-permanent display.
ja_pron: 1940-nen made ni, sore wa Nyūyōku no Kindai Bijutsukan ni ari, soko de han-eikyū-teki ni tenji saremashita.
native: By 1940, it was at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, where it stayed on semi-permanent display.

en: For the next 40 years.
zh: 接下來的40年。
ja: その後の40年間です。
local: For the next 40 years.
ja_pron: Sono ato no yonjū-nenkan desu.
native: For the next 40 years.

en: Picasso continued living in Nazi-occupied Paris.
zh: 畢卡索繼續住在納粹佔領的巴黎。
ja: ピカソはナチス占領下のパリに住み続けました。
local: Picasso continued living in Nazi-occupied Paris.
ja_pron: Pikaso wa Nachisu senryōka no Pari ni sumi tsudzukemashita.
native: Picasso continued living in Nazi-occupied Paris.

en: It is said that when a German officer visited him, he saw a photograph of Gernica on Picasso's war.
zh: 據說當一名德國軍官拜訪他時，他看到畢卡索的工作室裡有一張《格爾尼卡》的照片。
ja: ドイツの将校が彼を訪ねたとき、ピカソのアトリエにゲルニカの写真があるのを見たと言われています。
local: It is said that when a German officer visited him, he saw a photograph of Gernica on Picasso's war.
ja_pron: Doitsu no shōkō ga kare o tazuneta toki, Pikaso no atorie ni Gerunika no shashin ga aru no o mita to iwarete imasu.
native: It is said that when a German officer visited him, he saw a photograph of Gernica on Picasso's war.

en: He asked Picasso, did you do that?
zh: 他問畢卡索：是你做的嗎？
ja: 彼はピカソに尋ねました、「あなたがやったのですか？」と。
local: He asked Picasso, did you do that?
ja_pron: Kare wa Pikaso ni tazunemashita, 'Anata ga yatta no desu ka?' to.
native: He asked Picasso, did you do that?

en: Picasso replied, no, you did.
zh: 畢卡索回答：不，是你做的。
ja: ピカソは答えました、「いいえ、あなたがやったのです」と。
local: Picasso replied, no, you did.
ja_pron: Pikaso wa kotaemashita, 'Iie, anata ga yatta no desu' to.
native: Picasso replied, no, you did.

en: In New York, Gernica's fame grew.
zh: 在紐約，格爾尼卡的名聲增長了。
ja: ニューヨークで、ゲルニカの名声は高まりました。
local: In New York, Gernica's fame grew.
ja_pron: Nyūyōku de, Gerunika no meisei wa takamarimashita.
native: In New York, Gernica's fame grew.

en: And during the Vietnam War, it became a powerful anti-war symbol.
zh: 在越南戰爭期間，它成為強大的反戰象徵。
ja: そしてベトナム戦争中、それは強力な反戦の象徴となりました。
local: And during the Vietnam War, it became a powerful anti-war symbol.
ja_pron: Soshite Betonamu Sensō-chū, sore wa kyōryoku na hansen no shōchō to narimashita.
native: And during the Vietnam War, it became a powerful anti-war symbol.

en: In 1974, a protester defaced the painting with the words, kill lies all.
zh: 1974年，一名抗議者在畫上塗鴉寫下「kill lies all」字樣。
ja: 1974年、抗議者が絵に「kill lies all」という言葉を書き込みました。
local: In 1974, a protester defaced the painting with the words, kill lies all.
ja_pron: 1974-nen, kōgisha ga e ni 'kill lies all' to iu kotoba o kakikomimashita.
native: In 1974, a protester defaced the painting with the words, kill lies all.

en: It created international headlines.
zh: 這件事成為國際頭條新聞。
ja: それは国際的な見出しになりました。
local: It created international headlines.
ja_pron: Sore wa kokusaiteki na midashi ni narimashita.
native: It created international headlines.

en: Gernica was covered in heavy varnish, and the graffiti did no real damage at all.
zh: 格爾尼卡被厚厚的清漆覆蓋，塗鴉並未造成實質損害。
ja: ゲルニカは厚いニスで覆われており、落書きは実際には損害を与えませんでした。
local: Gernica was covered in heavy varnish, and the graffiti did no real damage at all.
ja_pron: Gerunika wa atsui nisu de ōwarete ori, rakugaki wa jissai ni wa songai o ataemasen deshita.
native: Gernica was covered in heavy varnish, and the graffiti did no real damage at all.

en: The fact that Gernica inspired such passions was a testament to its enduring power.
zh: 格爾尼卡激發如此強烈情感的事實證明了它持久的力量。
ja: ゲルニカがこれほどの情熱を呼び起こしたという事実は、その持続的な力の証です。
local: The fact that Gernica inspired such passions was a testament to its enduring power.
ja_pron: Gerunika ga kore hodo no jōnetsu o yobiokoshita to iu jijitsu wa, sono jizoku-teki na chikara no akashi desu.
native: The fact that Gernica inspired such passions was a testament to its enduring power.

en: Picasso died in 1973 at the age of 91.
zh: 畢卡索於1973年去世，享年91歲。
ja: ピカソは1973年に91歳で亡くなりました。
local: Picasso died in 1973 at the age of 91.
ja_pron: Pikaso wa 1973-nen ni 91-sai de nakunarimashita.
native: Picasso died in 1973 at the age of 91.

en: He had produced 50,000 works of art, including 1,885 paintings.
zh: 他創作了五萬件藝術作品，包括1885幅畫作。
ja: 彼は5万点の芸術作品を制作し、その中には1885点の絵画も含まれています。
local: He had produced 50,000 works of art, including 1,885 paintings.
ja_pron: Kare wa 5 man-ten no geijutsu sakuhin o seisaku shi, sono naka ni wa 1885-ten no kaiga mo fukumarete imasu.
native: He had produced 50,000 works of art, including 1,885 paintings.

en: While numerous worked by Picasso and masterpieces, Gernica stands alone.
zh: 雖然畢卡索有許多作品和傑作，但《格爾尼卡》獨樹一幟。
ja: ピカソの多くの作品や傑作がある中で、ゲルニカは唯一無二の存在です。
local: While numerous worked by Picasso and masterpieces, Gernica stands alone.
ja_pron: Pikaso no ōku no sakuhin ya kessaku ga aru naka de, Gerunika wa yuiitsu muni no sonzai desu.
native: While numerous worked by Picasso and masterpieces, Gernica stands alone.

en: Franco died in 1975, and with democracy restored, the painting's long exile was over.
zh: 佛朗哥於1975年去世，民主恢復後，這幅畫長久的流亡結束了。
ja: フランコは1975年に亡くなり、民主主義が回復すると、この絵の長い追放は終わりました。
local: Franco died in 1975, and with democracy restored, the painting's long exile was over.
ja_pron: Furanko wa 1975-nen ni nakunari, minshu shugi ga kaifuku suru to, kono e no nagai tsuihō wa owarimashita.
native: Franco died in 1975, and with democracy restored, the painting's long exile was over.

en: Even in the 21st century, Gernica was caused in controversy.
zh: 即使在21世紀，《格爾尼卡》仍引發爭議。
ja: 21世紀になっても、ゲルニカは論争を引き起こしました。
local: Even in the 21st century, Gernica was caused in controversy.
ja_pron: 21-seiki ni natte mo, Gerunika wa ronsō o hikiokoshimashita.
native: Even in the 21st century, Gernica was caused in controversy.

en: A tapestry of Gernica was put on display at the United Nations.
zh: 一幅《格爾尼卡》的掛毯在聯合國展出。
ja: ゲルニカのタペストリーが国連で展示されました。
local: A tapestry of Gernica was put on display at the United Nations.
ja_pron: Gerunika no tapesutorī ga Kokuren de tenji saremashita.
native: A tapestry of Gernica was put on display at the United Nations.

en: In 2003, then Secretary of State Colin Powell delivered a televised speech at the UN, arguing for war on Iraq.
zh: 2003年，時任國務卿柯林·鮑威爾在聯合國發表電視演說，主張對伊拉克開戰。
ja: 2003年、当時の国務長官コリン・パウエルは国連でテレビ演説を行い、イラク戦争を主張しました。
local: In 2003, then Secretary of State Colin Powell delivered a televised speech at the UN, arguing for war on Iraq.
ja_pron: 2003-nen, tōji no kokumu chōkan Korin Paueru wa Kokuren de terebi enzetsu o okonai, Iraku sensō o shuchō shimashita.
native: In 2003, then Secretary of State Colin Powell delivered a televised speech at the UN, arguing for war on Iraq.

en: In a form of blatant censorship, the Bush administration requested that the tapestry was covered up.
zh: 布希政府以明顯的審查形式要求將掛毯遮蓋起來。
ja: ブッシュ政権は露骨な検閲の形で、そのタペストリーを覆い隠すよう要請しました。
local: In a form of blatant censorship, the Bush administration requested that the tapestry was covered up.
ja_pron: Busshu seiken wa rokotsu na ken'etsu no katachi de, sono tapesutorī o ōikakusu yō yōsei shimashita.
native: In a form of blatant censorship, the Bush administration requested that the tapestry was covered up.

en: It is extraordinary that over 60 years after its completion, Gernica's message worried even the most powerful nation on earth.
zh: 令人驚訝的是，完成超過60年後，《格爾尼卡》的訊息仍讓地球上最強大的國家感到擔憂。
ja: 完成から60年以上経った今でも、ゲルニカのメッセージは地球上で最も強力な国さえも心配させています。
local: It is extraordinary that over 60 years after its completion, Gernica's message worried even the most powerful nation on earth.
ja_pron: Kansei kara rokujū-nen ijō tatta ima demo, Gerunika no messēji wa chikyū-jō de mottomo kyōryoku na kuni sae mo shinpai sasete imasu.
native: It is extraordinary that over 60 years after its completion, Gernica's message worried even the most powerful nation on earth.

en: No work of art in the 20th century has left its mark in quite the way Gernica has.
zh: 20世紀沒有任何藝術作品像《格爾尼卡》那樣留下深遠的影響。
ja: 20世紀のどの芸術作品も、ゲルニカほどの影響を残していません。
local: No work of art in the 20th century has left its mark in quite the way Gernica has.
ja_pron: 20-seiki no dono geijutsu sakuhin mo, Gerunika hodo no eikyō o nokoshite imasen.
native: No work of art in the 20th century has left its mark in quite the way Gernica has.

en: It has become the universal symbol of indiscriminate slaughter, and it has helped to shape a century.
zh: 它已成為無差別屠殺的普世象徵，並幫助塑造了一個世紀。
ja: それは無差別殺戮の普遍的な象徴となり、1世紀の形成に貢献しました。
local: It has become the universal symbol of indiscriminate slaughter, and it has helped to shape a century.
ja_pron: Sore wa musabetsu satsuriku no fuhenteki na shōchō to nari, isseiki no keisei ni kōken shimashita.
native: It has become the universal symbol of indiscriminate slaughter, and it has helped to shape a century.

en: The lessons of Gernica of universal suffering have still not been learnt, and that is why Gernica is just as important today as it was in 1937.
zh: 格爾尼卡關於普遍苦難的教訓仍未被學習，這就是為什麼格爾尼卡今天依然和1937年一樣重要。
ja: ゲルニカが伝える普遍的な苦しみの教訓はまだ学ばれておらず、だからこそゲルニカは1937年と同じくらい今日も重要なのです。
local: The lessons of Gernica of universal suffering have still not been learnt, and that is why Gernica is just as important today as it was in 1937.
ja_pron: Gerunika ga tsutaeru fuhenteki na kurushimi no kyōkun wa mada manabarete orazu, dakara koso Gerunika wa 1937-nen to onaji kurai kyō mo jūyō na no desu.
native: The lessons of Gernica of universal suffering have still not been learnt, and that is why Gernica is just as important today as it was in 1937.

en: Gernica is not just contemporary art. It is history.
zh: 《格爾尼卡》不僅是當代藝術，它是歷史。
ja: ゲルニカは単なる現代美術ではなく、歴史そのものです。
local: Gernica is not just contemporary art. It is history.
ja_pron: Gerunika wa tannaru gendai bijutsu de wa naku, rekishi sono mono desu.
native: Gernica is not just contemporary art. It is history.
